alex: Quick sync — proposing an "entropy-weighted" coalesce policy to help microburst p99s with minimal token-cost impact. Small canary ran this morning; summary below, want quick eyes before I open an RFC. @maria @sabrina

maria: Entropy-weighted? high level pls — how does it differ from randomized jitter we already have?

sabrina: Please paste the perf numbers and config you used. also any KV impact?

alex: Short: instead of uniform jitter, we sample delay from a distribution biased by recent arrival entropy (per-queue arrival-entropy over sliding window). high-entropy queues get shorter hold, low-entropy get slightly longer to improve coalescence. Idea: reduce correlated microburst waste while preserving KV locality for stable traffic.

alex: Canary details: 3 dedicated nodes, model: rwkv-large-ish (short seq), load: 2.5k QPS synthetic + real traffic mix. Duration: 45m.
- p50: ~unchanged (58ms -> 57ms)
- p95: -8% (210ms -> 193ms)
- p99: -23% (420ms -> 323ms)
- tokens/sec (cluster): -1.7%
- GPU util: +1.1% (more sustained due to larger batches)
- KV hit rate: -0.6ppt (98.4% -> 97.8%)
- kernel-swap events: +8% (short seq kernel thrash on some backends)

sabrina: KV drop small but visible. did evictions spike?

alex: Eviction rate up ~12% from baseline on those runs; mostly short-lived owing to slightly larger batch lead times. I think we can address via a small increase in KV capacity or prefer KV-preserving coalesces for cache-warm requests (see config).

alex: Config I used for canary (simplified):
```
coalesce: {
  window_ms: 8,
  jitter_mode: "entropy_weighted",
  entropy_window_ms: 2000,
  entropy_alpha: 0.7,
  max_hold_ms: 20,
  min_hold_ms: 1,
  kv_preserve_threshold: 0.7  # bias toward preserving KV if recent-hit-rate > 0.7
}
batching: {
  token_budget_target: 512,
  prefer_kernel: "short_seq_gemm_v2"
}
```

perf-bot: Canary run report: https://internal.perf/4087654321/entropy-scan — p99 improvement 23% (see plot). No SLA breaches during canary. Tags: #canary #coalesce #kv

jon: Two quick thoughts: 1) kernel-swap +8% could add jitter spikes downstream — add hysteresis on kernel selection to avoid flip-flopping. 2) add a short-term backoff if kv_eviction_rate > 0.2/s to prevent cascading misses.

alex: Agreed. For kernel hysteresis I implemented a 100ms sticky preference window so kernel swap needs sustained sequence-length shift to flip. Backoff rule I propose: if kv_eviction_rate > 0.25/s for >30s, reduce entropy_alpha by 0.4 (favors longer holds) and drop max_hold_ms by 25%.

kevin: Curious about model-side effects — does larger coalescing change prompt prefix cache usage for long contexts? any regressions there?

alex: Good catch. On long-context sessions (>1024 tokens) we saw negligible impact; prefix reuse still good since kv_preserve_threshold biases to preserve for high-hit flows. We'll monitor prefix_hit_ratio metric during rollout.

natalie: Rollout plan? metrics & guardrails?

alex: Plan: canary 5% for 1h (done), then 25% for 3h, 50% for 6h, full. Watchers/metrics: coalesce_avg_hold_ms, qlen_p95, p99_latency, tokens_per_sec, kv_hit_rate, kv_eviction_rate, kernel_swap_rate. Autorollback conditions: any of
- p99_latency increases >10% vs baseline for 5m
- kv_hit_rate drops >1.5ppt for 10m
- kv_eviction_rate >0.4/s for 3m
- kernel_swap_rate increase >25% sustained for 5m

alex: Next steps: open RFC with simulation of different entropy_alpha values + additional canary with kernel-hysteresis enabled. @sabrina can you add a few replay runs with live traffic replay 10x for 30m? @jon can you prototype eviction backoff rule in the runtime?

sabrina: Yep will schedule replays tonight, will post logs. :+1:

jon: I'll sketch the backoff patch and attach tests. target EOD.

alex: Thanks all. I'll draft RFC + rollout plan later today and include config toggles so we can A/B the entropy_weighted vs uniform jitter. Ping me if you want access to canary dashboards. :rocket:
